sources.entry: NymphCast - Turn your choice of Linux-capable hardware into an audio and video source for a television or powered speakers (alternative to Chromecast). (Source Code) BSD-3-Clause C++

summary.one_liner: NymphCast is an open-source C++ software suite that turns Linux-capable hardware into an audio and video receiver for TVs or powered speakers, serving as an alternative to Chromecast.
summary.what_it_does: NymphCast Server runs on a target device and receives audio/video streamed over the network from a client device or media server, or plays internet media (URL streaming) controlled by a client. The client side includes a CLI client, a Qt-based graphical NymphCast Player, and the LibNymphCast library/SDK. Playback uses FFmpeg for decoding and SDL2 for output, and the README says all codecs supported by FFmpeg are supported. Usage profiles exist for audio-only, audio/video, screensaver, and an experimental GUI "smart TV" mode. Multi-room synchronised playback is available through groups of receivers in the NymphCast Player. The server can also run AngelScript-based apps (preview status) and can show artist/title info on an LCDProc display.
use_cases: Stream local video or audio files from a phone or PC to a TV
Play internet media URLs on a receiver connected to speakers
Build a cheap Raspberry Pi or SBC media receiver for a TV
Synchronised multi-room audio across several receivers
Stream from a NymphCast MediaServer to a TV
Turn a Linux box into a Chromecast-style receiver
how_to_run: Download a pre-built release from the GitHub Releases page, or install the server package from your distro (e.g. pkg install NymphCast on FreeBSD)
Or build the server and client from source following the Setup Guides linked in the README
Run the server from the bin folder: ./nymphcast_server -c nymphcast_audio_config.ini
Open UDP and TCP port 4004 (and 4005 for MediaServer) in the firewall
Find receivers with the CLI client: nymphcast_client -r
notable: Acts as a Chromecast-style receiver that runs on user-supplied Linux hardware such as Raspberry Pi
Supports all FFmpeg-supported codecs and embedded bitmap subtitles such as PGS
Synchronised multi-room playback via groups of receivers in the NymphCast Player
Extensible via AngelScript-based NymphCast apps (preview) and a client SDK (LibNymphCast)
Client player runs on Windows, Linux, Android, FreeBSD and Haiku
caveats: Hardware-accelerated video decoding is limited or absent on several SBCs; Raspberry Pi 4 has no HEVC support per the README
Several features are experimental or partial: multi-room playback, SmartTV GUI mode, apps, and local media playback
Requires a client device for all modes except the GUI (Smart TV) mode
Text and external subtitles are planned for v0.2 and are not yet supported
keywords: send audio to tv over network
